root_cause.text: ibmasm_send_i2o_message() trusted the user-controlled dot_command_header fields used by get_dot_command_size() and used that computed length for memcpy_toio() without validating it against command->buffer_size, causing an out-of-bounds read from the command buffer in the ibmasm I2O message path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `command_size = get_dot_command_size(command->buffer); if (command_size > command->buffer_size) return 1;` before the copy, and the CVE/commit explicitly states the size “is derived from user-controlled fields in the dot_command_header ... and is never validated against the actual allocation size,” allowing `memcpy_toio()` to read up to ~65 KB past the allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate and bound the command size before building the I2O message to prevent oversized buffer use and limit the outgoing message to the supported maximum.
intent_record.what: The code changes the local variable `command_size` from `unsigned int` to `size_t`, moves its initialization to occur before acquiring an inbound MFA, adds a check that returns `1` if `get_dot_command_size(command->buffer)` exceeds `command->buffer_size`, adds a cap that clamps `command_size` to `I2O_COMMAND_SIZE` if larger, and updates the call to `outgoing_message_size()` to cast `command_size` back to `unsigned int`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this validates the parsed command length against the actual buffer size before using it, preventing oversized or inconsistent command lengths from being processed, and limits the I2O message payload size to the maximum allowed command size so the generated message header cannot describe an oversized transfer.

grouping_result.intent: Validate and bound the command size before building the I2O message to prevent oversized buffer use and limit the outgoing message to the supported maximum.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by validating and bounding the user-influenced command size before copying/building the I2O message, preventing use of a length that could exceed command->buffer_size and cause an out-of-bounds read.

candidates.rationale: This computes the copy length from user-controlled dot_command_header fields in command->buffer without validating that the derived size is within command->buffer_size, which is the root cause of the out-of-bounds read.
This propagates the unvalidated command_size into the outgoing I2O message construction, allowing an oversized message length derived from attacker-controlled input to be used downstream.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement derives command_size from user-controlled dot_command_header fields in command->buffer without checking that the resulting length is within command->buffer_size. That unvalidated size is later used for the I/O copy path, causing the out-of-bounds read root cause.

This statement propagates the previously unvalidated command_size into the constructed I2O message metadata, helping drive downstream use of an attacker-controlled oversized length in the message send path.
